description: Project foundation: install all missing npm packages, create globals.css with Tailwind v4 + shadcn CSS variable setup, create root layout.tsx, and establish all TypeScript types and core library files (utils, auth, demo-data, mock-analyzer, knowledge-base, scoring, resume-parser). This FEAT has no dependencies and must be completed before any other FEAT.
steps: Step 1 — Install missing packages. Run from C:/Users/kolte/AIresume/AI_ResumeAnalyzer: npm install recharts react-hook-form zod @hookform/resolvers uuid bcryptjs tw-animate-css shadcn cn && npm install -D @types/uuid @types/bcryptjs && npm install @radix-ui/react-dialog @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu @radix-ui/react-progress @radix-ui/react-scroll-area @radix-ui/react-separator @radix-ui/react-avatar @radix-ui/react-tooltip @radix-ui/react-select @radix-ui/react-accordion. Verify package.json lists all new packages.

Step 2 — Create app/globals.css with Tailwind v4 syntax. Use '@import tailwindcss'; '@import tw-animate-css'; '@import shadcn/tailwind.css'; then '@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))'; then '@theme inline { --color-background: var(--background); --color-foreground: var(--foreground); --color-card: var(--card); --color-card-foreground: var(--card-foreground); --color-popover: var(--popover); --color-popover-foreground: var(--popover-foreground); --color-primary: var(--primary); --color-primary-foreground: var(--primary-foreground); --color-secondary: var(--secondary); --color-secondary-foreground: var(--secondary-foreground); --color-muted: var(--muted); --color-muted-foreground: var(--muted-foreground); --color-accent: var(--accent); --color-accent-foreground: var(--accent-foreground); --color-destructive: var(--destructive); --color-border: var(--border); --color-input: var(--input); --color-ring: var(--ring); }'; then ':root { --radius: 0.625rem; all custom dark-navy app colors as oklch values mapped to the design tokens --background --card --border --primary --secondary etc. }'; then '@layer base { * { @apply border-border outline-ring/50; } body { @apply bg-background text-foreground; } }'. The app uses a deep navy dark theme: background #0a0f1e, card #0d1425, border #1e2d4a, primary #2563eb (electric blue), secondary #7c3aed (violet). Convert these hex values to oklch for the :root block.

Step 3 — Create app/layout.tsx as a Server Component. Import globals.css. Set metadata with title 'AI Resume Analyzer' and description. Render html+body with className 'dark' (to activate dark theme by default) and {children}. No 'use client'.

Step 4 — Create types/index.ts with ALL TypeScript interfaces: User { id, email, name, targetRole?, createdAt }, Resume { id, userId, filename, text, parsedData: ResumeData, createdAt }, ResumeData { name, email, phone, summary, skills, experience: WorkExperience[], education: Education[], projects: Project[], certifications, achievements, links }, WorkExperience { company, title, duration, bullets }, Education { institution, degree, field, year }, Project { name, description, techStack, url? }, Analysis { id, userId, resumeId, jobDescription, targetRole, overallScore, atsScore, jobMatchScore, skillsScore, contentScore, strengths, weaknesses, skillGaps: SkillGap[], atsSuggestions: ATSCheck[], contentSuggestions: ContentSuggestion[], resources: Resource[], projects: ProjectRecommendation[], careerActions, createdAt }, SkillGap { skill, importance: 'critical'|'high'|'medium', present: boolean, matchPercentage, reason, whatToDo }, ATSCheck { category, passed: boolean, message, suggestion }, ContentSuggestion { section, priority: 'high'|'medium'|'low', current, suggested, reason }, Resource { skill, title, type: 'course'|'article'|'video'|'book'|'practice', provider, url, free: boolean, difficulty: 'beginner'|'intermediate'|'advanced', duration }, ProjectRecommendation { title, description, techStack, impact, estimatedTime, resumeImpact }, AuthUser { id, email, name }, APIResponse<T> { success: boolean, data?: T, error?: string }. Files: types/index.ts

Step 5 — Create lib/utils.ts. Export cn() helper using clsx + tailwind-merge. This follows the shadcn/ui pattern: import { clsx, type ClassValue } from 'clsx'; import { twMerge } from 'tailwind-merge'; export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) { return twMerge(clsx(inputs)); }. Files: lib/utils.ts

Step 6 — Create lib/knowledge-base.ts. Define ROLE_SKILLS record mapping each of 6 roles (Data Analyst, AI/ML Engineer, Software Developer, Web Developer, Data Scientist, Business Analyst) to { critical: string[], high: string[], medium: string[] }. Define RESOURCES_DB: Record<string, Resource[]> mapping each skill to 2-3 real resources with real URLs (e.g., SQL: W3Schools, Mode Analytics SQL Tutorial, SQLZoo; Python: Python.org tutorial, Codecademy Python; Pandas: official docs; etc.). Define ATS_RULES array of rule objects with id/description/check pattern. Export all. Files: lib/knowledge-base.ts

Step 7 — Create lib/scoring.ts. Export computeAtsScore(resumeText: string, role: string): number using keyword_match(40%) + formatting checks(30%) + sections present(15%) + contact info(15%). Export computeJobMatchScore(resumeSkills: string[], roleSkills: { critical: string[], high: string[], medium: string[] }): number using required_skills(45%) + preferred(20%) + weighting. Export computeSkillsScore(matched: number, total: number): number. Export computeOverallScore(ats, jobMatch, skills, content): number with weights. Files: lib/scoring.ts

Step 8 — Create lib/mock-analyzer.ts. Export analyzeResume(resumeText: string, jobDescription: string, targetRole: string): Analysis. Logic: (a) normalize role to match ROLE_SKILLS keys; (b) extract skills from resumeText via keyword matching against all known skills; (c) compute scores using lib/scoring.ts functions; (d) build SkillGap[] for each required skill not found in resumeText; (e) build ATSCheck[] running each ATS rule against resumeText; (f) build ContentSuggestion[] by looking for weak phrases like 'responsible for', 'helped with', 'worked on' and suggesting quantified alternatives; (g) map each skill gap to 2-3 resources from RESOURCES_DB; (h) generate 3 ProjectRecommendation objects based on missing skills; (i) generate careerActions array. Return a fully populated Analysis object. This is deterministic — same input always produces same output. Files: lib/mock-analyzer.ts

Step 9 — Create lib/resume-parser.ts. Export parseResume(buffer: ArrayBuffer, mimeType: string): Promise<string>. For PDF: use pdfjs-dist with workerSrc set to node (import * as pdfjs from 'pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs' or the appropriate server-side import; pdfjs-dist v6 API). For DOCX: use mammoth.extractRawText({ buffer }). For TXT: decode buffer as UTF-8. Export extractResumeData(text: string): ResumeData using regex-based extraction for name (first line), email (email regex), phone (phone regex), sections (detect headers like EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, SKILLS, PROJECTS by all-caps lines or common header patterns). Files: lib/resume-parser.ts

Step 10 — Create lib/demo-data.ts. Export DEMO_RESUME: Resume (Alex Johnson, CS graduate, targeting Data Analyst role, with realistic work experience at a tech company, 3 projects, education at State University, skills including Python/JavaScript/HTML but MISSING SQL/Power BI/Statistics/Tableau/Pandas). Export DEMO_JOB: { description: string, role: 'Data Analyst' } (realistic job posting for Data Analyst at a fintech company requiring SQL, Python, Excel, Power BI, Statistics). Export DEMO_ANALYSIS: Analysis (pre-computed with overallScore:64, atsScore:58, jobMatchScore:61, skillsScore:45, contentScore:71, specific skillGaps for SQL/Power BI/Statistics/Pandas/Tableau, 6 resources, 3 projects, 5 careerActions, multiple ATSChecks with mixed pass/fail). Export DEMO_USER: AuthUser. Files: lib/demo-data.ts

Step 11 — Create lib/auth.ts. Export signJWT(userId: string): string using a simple base64-encoded payload (NOT a real JWT library — keep it lightweight for MVP: JSON.stringify({userId, exp: Date.now() + 7*24*60*60*1000}) then Buffer.from().toString('base64url')). Export verifyJWT(token: string): { userId: string } | null — decode and check expiry. Export AUTH_COOKIE_NAME = 'auth_token'. Export setAuthCookie(response: NextResponse, token: string): void and clearAuthCookie(response: NextResponse): void. Export getAuthCookie(request: NextRequest): string | null. Files: lib/auth.ts. NOTE: In Next.js 16, cookies() is async — but in API route handlers we read from request.cookies directly (synchronous on NextRequest), so use request.cookies.get(AUTH_COOKIE_NAME)?.value.
acceptance_criteria: app/globals.css imports tailwindcss correctly using Tailwind v4 '@import' syntax (not @tailwind directives)
types/index.ts compiles with zero TypeScript errors (run npm run build)
lib/mock-analyzer.ts.analyzeResume() returns a well-typed Analysis object with all required fields
lib/demo-data.ts exports match the Analysis type exactly
npm run build passes with zero errors after this FEAT

findings: 1) shadcn/tailwind.css import works — shadcn package exports ./tailwind.css pointing to ./dist/tailwind.css. 2) tw-animate-css exports style-only via 'tw-animate-css' (no .css suffix needed in CSS @import). 3) pdfjs-dist v6: DocumentInitParameters does NOT have 'isEvalSupported' — removed. TextContent items are 'TextItem | TextMarkedContent' — must use 'str' in item guard instead of direct type annotation. 4) mammoth.extractRawText expects Buffer not ArrayBuffer — must call Buffer.from(arrayBuffer) first. 5) uuid package works fine — uuidv4() from 'uuid'. 6) lib/auth.ts uses request.cookies.get() (sync) on NextRequest which is correct for Next.js 16 API routes — does NOT need async cookies(). 7) Next.js 16 build uses Turbopack — 'next build' does NOT emit a separate tsc check unless --no-turbo is used, but it does run TypeScript type checking as a separate step after compile. 8) All six role skill maps are defined in knowledge-base.ts; normalizeRole() covers common aliases. 9) DEMO_USER password is 'demo123' — later FEATs implementing auth API must hash this and store in the in-memory user store.
